h: The Kindness Beneath the Zeal of Pinchas

p: פִּנְחָס בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר כה, יא)
in his being zealous with My zeal in their midst, etc."
Now, one may examine this closely:
what is the expression "in their midst"?
גַּם מַה שֶּׁאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ (שָׁם יד-טו)
"And the name of the man of Yisrael, etc.,
and the name of the woman who was struck, etc."
why, at the time the incident was told,
רַק סְתָם אִישׁ מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳
only "a man of the Children of Yisrael, etc.,
while here it mentions their names?
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין פב, ב)
according to what is stated in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 82b),
that the tribes were disparaging him:
"Have you seen this son of Puti,
שֶׁפִּיטֵּם אֲבִי אִמּוֹ עֲגָלִים לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵּי
whose mother's father fattened calves for idolatry, etc.?"
The verse came and traced his lineage.
why did they not disparage him
from the time of Elazar's marriage
It should have traced his lineage from the start!
that the tribes were raising accusations
over this deed of his killing Zimri,
though he was not liable to death
and there is no obligation upon the zealots;
for they said (in the Gemara there, Sanhedrin 82a):
"One who comes to ask, we do not instruct him so";
רַק מִי שֶׁבּוֹעֵר בּוֹ קִנְאַת ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
only one in whom the zeal of Hashem of Hosts burns
And the tribes accused him over this,
that Moshe Rabbeinu did not kill him,
and no one was roused to kill him,
Presumably it is for the reason
that he is of the seed of Yisro,
who was the priest of Midian;
וְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (יִתְרוֹ, חֵלֶק ב סז, ב)
and it is stated in the holy Zohar (Yisro, II 67b):
there is a secret that is a king, etc.,
and beneath it there is a priest of iniquity, etc."
And the kelipah of Midian is anger,
that because he is of the seed of Yisro,
therefore he was roused to this zeal,
מַה שֶּׁלֹּא הָיָה עַל פִּי דִין
which was not according to the law.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ אֵצֶל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
as we find with Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
to pursue with so few men
and why should he have had
to risk his life for this?
the zeal of Hashem of Hosts burned in him
as is stated in the Midrash
(Rabbah 42:1 and Tanchuma, parshas Lech) on this:
עַל זֶה חֶרֶב פָּתְחוּ רְשָׁעִים (תְּהִלִּים לז, יד)
for there had not yet been war in the world,
and these came and opened with the sword, etc."
or for the sake of honor and the like.
Therefore the zeal of Hashem burned in him
as they said in the Midrash
אָמַר אַבְרָהָם זֶה קוֹנְיוֹן הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
and he goes out to war, etc."
to pursue and kill wicked men;
a prince of a tribe of Yisrael,
he is of the seed of the priest of Midian.
And in the Gemara there it is stated:
"Shaul: that he lent himself to sin."
That is, according to their exposition
that he was Shaul son of the Canaanite woman,
who was among those who went down to Egypt,
he was over two hundred fifty years old;
he certainly did not do this for his lust;
one no longer went out to the army.
Moreover, most of his years had already passed
so that it appears he was previously a tzaddik;
only because his tribe gathered against him,
And in the writings of the holy Arizal it is stated
that he had a connection to her
she was a reincarnation of Dinah,
and he was a reincarnation of Shechem.
that he need not have killed him,
because the trait of zealotry was in him,
מַה שֶּׁהָיָה מִזֶּרַע יִתְרוֹ כֹּהֵן מִדְיָן
from his being of the seed of Yisro the priest of Midian,
from the kelipah of anger, as mentioned above.
and traced his lineage to Aharon,
that on the contrary, his trait was the trait of kindness,
"in his being zealous with My zeal in their midst":
that at the time of the zeal
and only out of his great compassion for Yisrael
was he zealous with the zeal of Hashem of Hosts
וַעֲבוּר זֶה נָתַן לוֹ בְּרִיתוֹ שָׁלוֹם
and for this He gave him His covenant of peace.
And therefore it is mentioned here
"a prince of a father's house of the Shimonites."
וְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג רמב, ב)
And it is stated in the holy Zohar (this parshah, III 242b)
וְחָשַׁב נָשִׂיא נֶגֶד מִדַּת כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
and counts "prince" opposite the attribute of Keser Elyon
(and so it writes in the Ra'aya Mehemna
from the ten sefiros in their order,
and counts princes opposite Keser Elyon);
and likewise, on the opposite side, she was
the daughter of Tzur, "head of the peoples" (Bamidbar 25:15),
"the daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister,"
for she was from the beginning of the kelipah.
there was the accusation against him from the tribes;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נָתַן לוֹ בְּרִיתוֹ שָׁלוֹם
and Hashem Yisbarach gave him His covenant of peace,
that it was only with the trait of kindness,
